subject.name: Lawrence Gerard Nassar
subject.publicSummary: Former physician and USA Gymnastics official convicted in federal and Michigan courts of child-exploitation and criminal sexual-conduct offenses.

powerRoles.title: Osteopathic physician and associate professor
powerRoles.sourceLabel: DOJ OIG testimony describing Nassar's employment and medical role

powerRoles.title: National Medical Coordinator and treating physician
powerRoles.sourceLabel: DOJ OIG testimony describing Nassar's USA Gymnastics role

records.title: Federal child-pornography and obstruction convictions
records.summary: Nassar pleaded guilty to receiving and possessing child pornography and destroying or concealing evidence, and was sentenced to 60 years in federal prison.
records.sourceLabel: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Michigan — federal sentencing release
records.jurisdiction: Western District of Michigan, United States
records.outcome: Sixty-year federal prison sentence, consecutive to state sentences.
records.rightOfReply: Nassar entered guilty pleas; no contrary final disposition was located in the reviewed official sources.
records.counterEvidence: The federal judgment covers child-pornography and obstruction offenses; separate state records address hands-on sexual assaults.
records.proofNeeded: A court order vacating or reversing the federal convictions would change this classification.
records.boundary: This record is limited to the federal counts and sentence.

records.title: Michigan first-degree criminal sexual-conduct convictions
records.summary: DOJ OIG records state that Nassar pleaded guilty in Michigan state court to seven counts of first-degree criminal sexual conduct and that federal and state convictions produced sentences exceeding 100 years.
records.sourceLabel: DOJ Office of Inspector General — testimony summarizing federal and state prosecutions
records.outcome: Guilty pleas to seven first-degree criminal sexual-conduct counts; lengthy consecutive state sentences followed.
records.rightOfReply: Nassar pleaded guilty; victim-impact and sentencing proceedings are part of the public record.
records.counterEvidence: This summary relies on the DOJ OIG's official account and does not reproduce unnecessary victim details.
records.proofNeeded: A later Michigan appellate or post-conviction order altering the judgments would change this classification.
records.boundary: Limited to Nassar's own adjudicated Michigan offenses; institutions and employees require separate evidence and classification.
